steps.step: Pick coverage band, select and packetise the words

steps.owner: manager (this run) - reading passes move to Shawn from step 7
steps.note: 244 nulls read, 5 false (2.05%). null-auditor spawned BY NAME, unlike entry-reader.

9 senses / 6 entries repaired third-hand; blind re-read 17/17 right, rank_wrong 0. SPLIT NOT HELD: shawn unavailable 2026-09-04, so the manager session wrote the repairs and orchestrated the read - different-model-fresh-context, as 006-011 ran.

778 entries / 78 packets. Ranker 778/778 accepted (one packet re-run for a dropped synset id). Enricher 766 accepted, 12 rejected (1.5%), 1,998 senses, 1,903 null / 95 candidate. ~3.7M tokens. Run by the MANAGER, not shawn - see blocked-entries.json for the 12 and for the two defects they expose (lexicon irregular inflections; enricher.md s1 learner-length floor).

77 of 766 entries (10.1%, seed 705), 194 senses. 3.09% sense defect, rank_wrong 0, 1 unsure - against the pilot's 3.14% and a 10% halt line. 6 faults: 2 example-wrong-sense, 2 'other' (a badly cut book quote and an invented example that is not idiomatic English), 1 label-unjustified, 1 learner-narrowed. Read from a SCRATCH batch; batch-0001.jsonl untouched, so step 9 is unaffected. Split NOT held (manager authored and orchestrated).

6 senses repaired third-hand from the 10% read's faults. Blind re-read: 15 of 16 right; the one miss was the repairing hand's own (truth reused the neighbouring sense's example). Re-repaired and re-read clean. Validator unchanged at 766/12.

Blocked on first run by a collision the merge had no rule for: stage 7's Enricher answered neutral on 10 senses an earlier hand had charged. 5 errored (batch-0001 explanations on hope n+v, run, hold, understand); 5 were SILENT (eagerly, highly x2, perfectly, seriously - inherited adverb charges), keeping their tone and their seat on a charged family spectrum under a neutral label. Adjudicated blind by null-auditor (fable), never the authoring hand: 9/9 null-right, plus hope.v already null-right in the pilot audit. The 3 whose evidence packet the auditor itself called unrepresentative (highly x2, perfectly - the book uses only the intensifier sense) were re-read on an on-sense packet: 3/3 null-right again. Repaired by dropping the 5 refuted explanations from batch-0001.overlay and adding the 5 adverb senses to adverb-deny.json. dict_enrich_apply.py now records the disagreement at the merge, where both hands are still visible, so a later neutral over an earlier charge halts instead of half-halting. Lexicon defect from step 7 fixed here as blocked-entries.json planned: do->does (the -o rule's len>2 guard excluded the only two two-letter -o verbs; 'does' had been resolving to *doe*, the deer) and 456 -man/-woman plurals incl. women/gentlemen. derived-bulk regenerated: 454 entries changed, every change a pure addition, entry count identical, swn coverage 97.7%. That cleared 3 of the 12 blocked entries: 769 accepted / 9 rejected / 2006 senses (was 766/12/1998). The 9 remaining rejects are all the rubric-collision class, as recorded.

dict_pipeline --no-build: 3857 entries, 0 errors, 5924 warnings (near-duplicate glosses, the standing class). entry_validate --refresh: 3857 entries / 14375 senses, clean - every sense traceable, POS agrees, gloss unchanged; 0 errors, 0 warnings.

steps.step: Done-check: app opens offline, a book word returns a readable entry
steps.note: PASSES ON A FRESH INSTALL. Pixel_10_Pro AVD, Android 17, airplane mode on and ping 8.8.8.8 'Network is unreachable'. App launches cold (3.8s) with no crash, and a word sent by ACTION_SEND - the path a book reader actually uses - returns a readable entry. countenance shows the learner line ('the look that a person's face gives') and the book's own sentence about Mr. Bingley; amiable shows the POSITIVE badge, its tone note and the full family spectrum on the mocking->warm axis; does resolves to do with 'does - third-person singular of do'. 78 engine unit tests pass. FOUND WHILE CHECKING - a shipping defect, recorded as stage 7 issue 1 below: the first run of the check silently read a two-day-old dictionary. DictRepository.installBundledIfNeeded copies a bundled dictionary once and guards it with a .installed-<dir> marker, so an EXISTING user who upgrades the APK keeps their old popup-en for ever and never receives book one. Confirmed on device: 11,828,099 B from 2026-09-03 where the new build is 12,035,397 B; pm clear then relaunch installed the new one and the learner lines appeared. Per-dictionary colour, order and enabled state live in DictRegistry keyed by file path, NOT in the dictionary files, so re-copying would not disturb them - the marker's only real job is to keep a dictionary the user DELETED from coming back.

stages.role_rule: The hand that writes is never the hand that reads, and it is now enforced across sessions, not just across models. The manager authored the pilot 100 and has seen every ranker and enricher rationale, so it is contaminated for those entries and must not read them. Neither session has seen the 778, so whichever one does not author it can read it honestly.

issues.title: A bundled dictionary is never refreshed after the first install
issues.impact: book one reaches new installs only. Every existing user upgrades the APK and keeps the old dictionary, so the whole of stage 7 is invisible to them.
issues.proposed_fix: keep the marker as the 'user deleted this, do not bring it back' signal, but record the bundled .ifo (wordcount, synwordcount, idxfilesize - all of which move with content) in it and re-copy when the bundled .ifo differs AND the dictionary directory still exists.
